edges.description: Phagocytosis of M. tuberculosis triggers type I interferon signaling, which induces GBP4 expression as a host-directed restriction mechanism.
Infected macrophages differentiate into foamy macrophages which form the cellular core of TB granulomas.
Granuloma necrosis leads to cavitation and destruction of lung parenchyma.
NETs contribute to immunopathology, tissue injury, and relapse risk in TB.
Drug-resistant TB strains render standard treatment regimens ineffective, leading to persistent infection and continued disease transmission.
Alveolar macrophages and epithelial cells take up Mtb, reproducing the initial uptake step in a human alveolar microenvironment.
edges.limitations: The macrophage compartment is iPSC-derived rather than tissue-resident alveolar macrophage, and the chip carries no recruited neutrophils or lymphocytes, so uptake occurs without the wider cellular context of a human alveolus.
edges.source: Autologous iPSC-derived alveolus-on-chip (iLoC) Mtb infection model

edges.description: A macrophage-restricted ATG14 knockout tests the autophagy requirement directly. The result refines the usual framing: ATG14 loss raised macrophage necrosis without permitting bacterial replication, separating autophagy's role in host-cell survival from its role in bacterial restriction.
edges.limitations: ATG14 is not GBP4, and the chip result speaks to the autophagy machinery this node invokes rather than to GBP4 specifically. The perturbation is also a complete knockout rather than the partial, regulated variation seen in human infection.
edges.source: Autologous iPSC-derived alveolus-on-chip (iLoC) Mtb infection model

edges.description: Large macrophage aggregates with a necrotic core arose stochastically and supported focal Mtb replication, an early necrotic-aggregate structure resembling the initiating step of granuloma formation.
edges.limitations: These aggregates are not granulomas. They lack lymphocytic cuffing, epithelioid and multinucleate giant-cell differentiation, and fibrotic encapsulation, form only stochastically, and arise over days rather than the weeks of granuloma maturation in vivo. The chip has no adaptive immune compartment, so the T-cell-dependent stages cannot occur at all.
edges.source: Autologous iPSC-derived alveolus-on-chip (iLoC) Mtb infection model

edges.description: Foci of aggregated cell death progressed to severe disruption of both the epithelial and endothelial layers, reproducing the barrier destruction that underlies tuberculous tissue damage.
edges.limitations: Damage is confined to the two cellular layers on the chip; there is no matrix remodelling, cavitation, or vascular thrombosis, which are central to tissue damage in human pulmonary tuberculosis.
edges.source: Autologous iPSC-derived alveolus-on-chip (iLoC) Mtb infection model

edges.description: Neither macrophages nor epithelial cells were permissive to Mtb replication, in contrast to conventional two-dimensional cultures where Mtb replicates within 48 hours and to human disease where progressive intracellular replication is the norm. The chip therefore does not reproduce sustained evasion of intracellular killing, and replication appeared only in rare necrotic foci.
edges.limitations: Non-permissiveness may reflect the immaturity of iPSC-derived macrophages, the absence of the immunosuppressive signals of an established lesion, or the short observation window, rather than a genuine property of the human alveolus. Until that is resolved, the model should not be used to score evasion phenotypes or to screen compounds whose readout is restriction of intracellular replication.
edges.source: Autologous iPSC-derived alveolus-on-chip (iLoC) Mtb infection model

nodes.description: A single-donor human iPSC-derived lung-on-chip containing alveolar type 1 and type 2 epithelial cells, vascular endothelial cells, and iPSC-derived macrophages, under air-liquid interface with three-dimensional cyclic stretch. Because every cell type derives from one donor, the model is autologous and genetically tractable: an ATG14 knockout confined to the macrophage compartment can be combined with wild-type epithelium and endothelium to isolate a cell-type-specific autophagy requirement, which is not achievable in a patient or in a whole-animal knockout.

nodes.description: Development of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) TB through genetic mutations that confer resistance to first-line and second-line antitubercular drugs, driven by ineffective treatment regimens and irregular antibiotic exposure.

evidence.reference_title: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis: a comprehensive review of pathogenesis, drug resistance, current treatment and future prospects.
evidence.snippet: There is also a discussion of the MTB lineage and the mutant types. The mechanisms of multidrug resistance and ineffective treatment regimens have driven advances in drug development and alternative therapeutics.

nodes.description: Type I interferon-inducible GBP4 (guanylate-binding protein 4) mediates autophagy-dependent restriction of Mycobacterium tuberculosis through a TRIM21-dependent autophagy pathway that prevents SORT1-mediated progranulin degradation. This activates TFEB and FOXO3a, driving lysosomal acidification and phagosome-lysosome fusion to enhance intracellular bacterial killing.

evidence.reference_title: Human GBP4 promotes TRIM21-BIP-dependent autophagy to restrict M. tuberculosis infection by preventing SORT1-mediated progranulin degradation.
evidence.snippet: Our study uncovers a key role for GBP4 in regulating cell-autonomous resistance in human macrophages and may facilitate the development of host-directed therapies against tuberculosis

evidence.reference_title: Cavitary tuberculosis: the gateway of disease transmission.
evidence.snippet: Cavitation is a dangerous consequence of pulmonary tuberculosis associated with poor outcomes, treatment relapse, higher transmission rates, and development of drug resistance.

evidence.reference_title: Hypoxia and tissue destruction in pulmonary TB.
evidence.snippet: Human TB lesions are severely hypoxic and M.tb drives HIF-1α accumulation, synergistically increasing collagenase activity which will lead to lung destruction and cavitation.
Pulmonary cavitation with cough-generated aerosol is the principle means of spread, and lung remodeling (healed cavitation, fibrosis, and bronchiectasis) is a major cause of lung disability.

evidence.snippet: After many months, the affected lung suddenly undergoes caseation necrosis with vanishingly few MTB. The necrotic tissue fragments to produce a cavity or hardens to develop fibrocaseous disease.
